newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian radio criticises Netanyahu, U.S..
newsitem.headline: Syrian radio criticises Netanyahu, U.S..

text.p: Syria's state-run radio on Friday accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the United States of escalating tension and creating a state of frustration in the Middle East.

The radio, which reflects government thinking, said the despair was caused by Netanyahu's policies including his decision to build several thousand houses for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem, and a U.S. veto last week which blocked a U.N. Security Council resolution demanding Israel halt the building.
The radio did not refer directly to the killing of seven Israeli schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier on Thursday but said:
"Practices of the Netanyahu government contradicted the bases of the peace process, dimmed all hopes and escalated tension.
"The recent incidents reflected the feeling of outrage and bitterness."
A Jordanian soldier on Thursday shot and killed seven Israeli schoolgirls who were on a field trip to an Israeli-Jordanian border site called "the island of peace".

"The Netanyahu government is making public its determination to keep the occupied Arab lands and to expel the Arab citizens. The brokers of the peace process (the United States) did support their initiative and allowed Israel to direct stabs against it," the radio said.

"It (United States) dealt with the region with double standards and the result was the deterioration of the peace process, the collapse of the international credibility and the escalation of Israeli hostility," it said.
Syria had strongly condemned Israel's approval of plans to build 6,500 housing units in East Jerusalem, claimed by Palestinians as the capital of a state they hope to build.
Syria has held sporadic peace negotiations with Israel since 1991 but the talks were blocked over the fate of the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967. No talks have been held for the past year.
